content: 1. Evaluate whether the target, expressed as a fraction (n/13), has been met. 2. Utilize the 2023–2027 health facility family planning standards to assess outpatient health facility family planning impact indicators. 3. Determine the number of contraceptive doses administered or prescribed in outpatient settings by analyzing routine Health Management Information System (HMIS) data. If HMIS data is unavailable, use facility register observations as outlined in Checklist 5. 4. Record data for each level of outpatient facility, including: a) National and regional hospitals, b) First-level referral hospitals, and c) First-level facilities. 5. Calculate the couple-years of protection provided by contraceptive methods such as intrauterine devices (IUDs) and oral contraceptive pills (OCPs). 6. Use representative population-based surveys, such as the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) or the Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS), to periodically measure family planning intervention coverage. 7. Monitor adolescent birth rates and contraceptive usage trends, including IUDs and OCPs, to inform program planning. 8. Develop an annual implementation plan for improving family planning services by identifying priority problems. 9. Review checklist summary tables from Section 3, which should be displayed on flip-chart paper and posted on the wall. These include: a) Essential medicines and supplies (Checklist 3), b) Policies, standards, and guidelines (Checklist 4), c) Facility contraceptive usage and targets (Checklist 5), and d) Staff coaching (Checklist 7). 10. Analyze findings from checklists and monitoring and evaluation tables, noting differences between various levels of outpatient facilities. 11. Identify technical issues or gaps in service delivery and determine the underlying reasons for these gaps. 12. Summarize the final list of prioritized areas for improvement and ensure group consensus. Record these prioritized areas under each relevant program area. 13. Develop an annual family planning action plan by reviewing actions from the previous year’s plan and identifying whether current actions need to be continued. Brainstorm new actions to address priority areas for improvement. 14. Base priority actions on the underlying reasons for gaps in service delivery, considering: a) The importance of improving family planning clinical practices, b) Whether actions can be implemented with existing resources and personnel, and c) Whether actions can be initiated within the next three months (or, for longer-term priorities, whether initial steps can begin within three months). 15. Write the agreed-upon priority actions on the flip-chart for further planning and implementation.
